name: hint-shows-on-a-held-row
description: Hint bubble spec, hold trigger: a tab row held past HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS (500ms) with the pointer still on it shows 'Hold to open in a peek', and pointerup hides it. The runner has no separate down/up scenario action, so the gesture is dispatched the same way chrome-row-controls.json presses a button: a PointerEvent from an eval, read straight off the row's own getBoundingClientRect() rather than a hardcoded pixel pair, because row heights move pixel clicks (memory note) but not a DOM-targeted dispatch. The hold trigger is element-anchored, so hint.js's native branch sends it to HintOverlayWidget instead of rendering it in the sidebar document - the bubble reads land on the /hint route, not /sidebar.

actions.note: ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
the hold hint is gated off by default, this dataset flag turns it on lazily at show time

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.row.tabrow'); if (!row) { return 'no-row'; } const r = row.getBoundingClientRect(); const cx = r.left + r.width / 2; const cy = r.top + r.height / 2; row.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown', {clientX: cx, clientY: cy, bubbles: true})); return 'pressed'; })()
actions.note: down at the row's own center, read from its live rect
past HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS (500ms) on the real clock

actions.expected: Hold to open in a peek
actions.note: element-anchored, so hint.js's native branch routes it through chrome.send to HintOverlayWidget's own /hint document rather than rendering in the sidebar - the widget is lazily built on first show, hence the poll

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.row.tabrow'); if (!row) { return 'no-row'; } const r = row.getBoundingClientRect(); const cx = r.left + r.width / 2; const cy = r.top + r.height / 2; row.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', {clientX: cx, clientY: cy, bubbles: true})); return 'released'; })()
(() => { window.atriumShowHint({text: 'corner probe', keys: '', anchor: {left: 300, top: 300, width: 60, height: 20}, ttlMs: 8000}); return 'shown'; })()
actions.note: a fixed, already-resolved anchor (the /hint route's own showHint() takes {left,top,width,height} directly, the same shape HintOverlayWidget::PushPending sends - see hint.js place()) instead of another row hold, so the bubble's top-left corner lands at a KNOWN pixel (left=300, top=300+20+8=328, GAP_PX=8) rather than wherever this fixture's row happens to sit. The widget is already built from the gesture above; a second Show() just repositions it.

assertions.expected: Hold to open in a peek
assertions.desc: AC: the hold trigger's bubble text, past HOLD_THRESHOLD_MS with the pointer still on the row
AC: the bubble renders at a real width, not clipped to nothing
AC: the bubble paints a surface, not a transparent box
the fixed-anchor bubble rendered so the corner probe below reads a real frame

assertions.label: the-card-is-painted
assertions.desc: THE CONTROL: 30px right, 11px down from the bubble's top-left corner (left=300,top=328) - inside the card, past the pill's rounded end on any bubble wider than a couple words. --ov-paper is near-white, so this reads light and confirms the capture caught the bubble.

assertions.label: the-corner-shows-the-page
assertions.desc: 50px outside the bubble's top-left corner (left=300,top=328) - past --ov-shadow's 36px blur, so this is clear of the card's own drop shadow and reads only the canvas. A body that stays opaque paints white there regardless of what is underneath; devbar's equivalent widget-painted-a-square regression read near 233 (the-devbar-corners-show-the-dark-page.json).
